reason: The premise that K1 is not an independent retry after a K2-only timeout ignores #35. #35 = exp57b = x138 + the same DaughterNet insertion scored COMPLETE 0.954 on the same hidden run, with L35 in (6.72, 7.73] h (poll.log l.3138). K1 = exp57b + safetail, which adds gates only, and its dummy CSV sha equals exp57b. P36 (ungated insertion) also completed in <= 7.42 h. The shared 8.0/9.5 h timers only act above 8 h, so saying 'K1 shares both timers' would push the user away from the one retry whose code path has already finished on the hidden data about 4.3 h under the limit. With the twin completing, a K2-only timeout points to lowrefine x insertion, which K1 lacks, or to a platform/hardware draw, where any resubmit is a fresh draw. Either way K1 is the best-supported retry. What remains of the finding is already in the rules: C3 + V1 (CONTEXT l.2029/2036) already give {twin #38, exp52} when there is no K1. V3 already limits K2'' to the runtime trigger with B > 9.0 h, and a timeout gives it less margin. The event has probability < ~1%. No change is justified, and the proposed wording is misleading.
fix: No rule change. If C2(d) ever fires (timeout/compute on K2 only), the question to the user should say: 'K1 is essentially #35 (x138 + insertion), which finished on the hidden run in <= 7.73 h; K1 [OK] is the default retry. The no-new-submit alternative is the C3/V1 pair {twin #38, exp52}. Do not offer K2'' after a timeout.' Do not describe K1 as sharing the failure mode.
realistic_gain: ~0 (the event has probability < ~1%, and the proposed wording, if adopted, would slightly bias the user against the evidence-backed retry)
